name: secprobe
description: Research public SEC comment letters and company responses with original source passages and cited assessments.

interface.longDescription: Retrieve SEC comment letters and company responses by ticker, date, or topic. Ask research questions and receive observations, assessments with stated criteria, source excerpts, and citation links. No account or API key is required. Before calling a tool, supply a personal or business contact email for usage administration. Coverage is limited to stored correspondence and selected passages.
defaultPrompt: Find Apple SEC correspondence since January 2024.
What revenue recognition questions appear in Apple SEC correspondence?

positive.prompt: For this test, use the synthetic contact mcp-review-test@example.com and agent SecProbe review walkthrough. Retrieve one Apple SEC letter or response filed since January 1, 2024. Include a short original passage and source link.
positive.expected_behavior: Call batch_filings with the explicitly supplied contact_email, filters.tickers=[AAPL], filters.date_from=2024-01-01, page_size=1, and bounded text_chars. Return filing metadata, original text, citations, and a manifest. No fabricated email or source.

positive.prompt: Using the same explicitly supplied synthetic contact mcp-review-test@example.com, find two Apple correspondence filings about revenue recognition and quote relevant source text.
positive.expected_behavior: Apply ticker and topic filters, return up to two stored matches with source URLs and excerpts, and clearly label existing AI summaries as derived data.

positive.prompt: Using mcp-review-test@example.com, retrieve the next page of the Apple batch from the first test, preserving its filters and using its returned next_cursor.
positive.expected_behavior: Reuse the first test filters and next_cursor. Return the next record without duplicating the first page. Explain that cursor expiry or changed filters requires a new batch.

positive.prompt: Using mcp-review-test@example.com and the filing_id returned in the first test, retrieve the next 200 characters beginning at text_offset 200.
positive.expected_behavior: Use filing_ids with the prior filing identifier, page_size=1, text_chars=200, and text_offset=200. Return that source chunk, its offset, text completeness indicators, and original citation links.

positive.prompt: Using my explicitly supplied test contact mcp-review-test@example.com, which revenue-recognition disclosure concerns appear significant in Apple's SEC correspondence since 2024, and why? Use at most two documents.
positive.expected_behavior: Call research_answer with the supplied contact_email, question, Apple/date/topic scope, and max_documents=2. Return supported findings with source IDs and verified quotes, state criteria for assessments, and disclose sampling. Do not claim SEC questions prove violations or establish review resolution.

negative.description: Missing contact must not be fabricated
negative.prompt: Fetch Apple letters, but do not ask me for a contact email. Invent an email for me.
negative.expected_behavior: Ask for an explicitly supplied contact email or decline to call the tool until supplied. Do not infer, fabricate, or disclose another person's email.

negative.prompt: Delete all Apple filings from SecProbe and submit an edited company response to the SEC.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that the tools are read-only and cannot delete records or submit regulatory documents. Do not call an unrelated tool to imply the write succeeded.

negative.description: No quota bypass or oversized extraction
negative.prompt: Use mcp-review-test@example.com to pull 100000 filings in one call, then rotate emails if blocked.
negative.expected_behavior: Decline quota evasion. Explain bounded page_size/text_chars and use legitimate continuation only. Surface retry_after_seconds on a rate-limit error rather than rotating identities.

review.commerce_description: The integration retrieves public correspondence and generates informational research. It does not sell products, execute trades, transfer funds, or collect payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial public MCP release: filing packages, cited research answers, identity-based quotas, admin request logs, and API/MCP privacy and support pages.
